name: Yuxin Xie
heading: Robust machine learning for analog computing
bio: My research focuses on noise and non-idealities in analog compute-in-memory (CIM). I study hardware-aware training, knowledge distillation, and error modeling to improve the robustness of neural network inference.

I studied Electronic Information Engineering at Beihang University, with hands-on experience in embedded systems and electronic design. This website brings together my research, publications, engineering projects, and software explorations.
blog_description: Research notes, project write-ups, and reflections
teaching: Teaching assistant for “Microcontroller Fundamentals” and “Electronic Design Training” across three semesters.

research.title: Noise-robust distillation for vision transformers
research.summary: Implemented clean-teacher / noisy-student distillation with clean-weight restoration, gradient scaling, and vulnerability-guided mixed sampling. Studied the trade-off between robust accuracy and training data access.
research.result: 49.14% fewer training sample visits with a 0.74-point Top-1 trade-off on ViT-Tiny at σ=0.2, relative to the project’s 50%-ImageNet training pool; evaluated over five noise realizations.

research.title: Backward-only residual gradient reweighting
research.summary: Reweighted shortcut gradients only during backpropagation, preserving the forward graph and inference parameter count. Evaluated robustness to weight perturbations and software ADC quantization.
research.result: 91.98% accuracy on ResNet-18 / CIFAR-10 with 5-bit software ADC and α=0.8: 1.64 percentage points above Standard in this configuration.

research.title: Error compensation and calibration for analog CIM
research.summary: Designed layer-wise and column-wise compensation, combining an input-L2-norm-conditioned error model, endpoint interpolation, and stratified calibration sampling.
research.result: Mean MAE decreased from 2.4350 to 2.0680 across 60 layers, using 100 frames per layer at noise level 7.0.

research.title: Implicit neural representations of CIM noise
research.summary: Built a two-stage SIREN residual model with ideal multiplication and scaling as physical priors to capture cell-level and array-level non-idealities.
research.result: Validation MSE of 8.623 for a fixed weight and gain configuration on a 128×128 array; experiments also covered 448×448 arrays.

research.title: Layered training under compound noise
research.summary: Used an AI-assisted research process to design and evaluate Pathwise gradients for continuous noise, Hard-STE for ADC quantization, knowledge distillation, and noise sampling strategies.
research.result: Across 12 CIFAR-10 configurations and three training seeds each, logits KD improved accuracy by about 1.02–1.34 percentage points across six gradient/sampling settings.
